text: The fundamental reason a nonlinear activation is hard to implement in optics is that photons essentially do not interact with each other at the low powers that make photonic computing attractive.
explanation: True: the book states 'the activation is the hard part because photons do not interact.' Material nonlinearities (Kerr, saturable absorption, free-carrier, gain saturation) exist but demand optical powers orders of magnitude above the femtojoule budgets, which is why opto-electronic activation is the pragmatic answer.
